title: Testing
outcome: Build a testing strategy that proves pure rules, service orchestration, repositories, HTTP contracts, frontend behavior, and critical browser flows at the right cost.
artifact: Vitest + integration + Playwright test suite with deterministic fixtures and CI-ready commands.
labSteps: List the highest-risk TaskFlow behaviors before choosing test counts.
Write a pure unit test for one deterministic business policy.
Test a service with controlled dependencies and assert business outcome rather than private calls.
Run a repository integration test against real PostgreSQL with isolated data.
Run an API test through NestJS for validation/auth/error contract.
Write one Playwright flow for a critical user journey and make setup/cleanup reproducible.
failureModes: Mocking the thing the test is supposed to prove
Huge number of brittle snapshot/UI implementation tests
Shared mutable test data causing order-dependent failures
E2E used for every rule, making feedback too slow
mastery: Can choose test level by risk
Can test real persistence when needed
Can explain what each test does not prove
principles: Use unit tests for focused behavior, integration tests for collaborating infrastructure, and end-to-end tests for critical user flows.
Test business outcomes and contracts rather than coupling every test to private implementation details.
Keep tests deterministic by controlling clocks, random values, external services, and database state where necessary.
A useful test suite catches regressions while remaining fast enough to run continuously in development and CI.
